## Data Setup

Import downloaded raw CSV data.

Convert to R-friendly variable names using the `janitor` package, and force data to classic tibble structure (instead of `spc_tbl_` )

```{r}
mxmh_raw <- read_csv("data/mxmh_survey_results.csv")
mxmh_raw <- janitor::clean_names(as_tibble(mxmh_raw))
str(mxmh_raw)
```

Basic data cleaning (assign categorical data as factors).

```{r}
mxmh <- mxmh_raw |>
  mutate(
    #Nominal factors:
    primary_streaming_service = as.factor(primary_streaming_service),
    fav_genre =as.factor(fav_genre),
    #Yes/No categorical:
    across(c("while_working", "instrumentalist", "composer", "exploratory", "foreign_languages"),
           function(x) factor(x, levels=c("Yes", "No"))),
    #Freq categorical:
    across(starts_with("frequency_"),
           function(x) factor(x, levels=c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Very frequently"))),
    #Effect categorical:
    music_effects = factor(music_effects, levels=c("Improve", "No effect", "Worsen"))
  )

str(mxmh)
```


## Numeric EDA

**Contingency Tables**

Use tidy summary methods with results stored in tibbles. This will simplify reporting on the app.

One-Way:

```{r}
mxmh |> 
  drop_na(fav_genre) |>
  group_by(fav_genre) |>
  summarize(count=n(), .groups = "drop")
```

Two-Way:

```{r}
mxmh |> 
  drop_na(fav_genre, composer) |>
  group_by(fav_genre, composer) |>
  summarize(count=n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = composer, values_from=count)
```

**Summary Stats** 

Again, use tidy methods with tibble result storage to simplify the app. I chose to report mean, sd, min, median, max.

```{r}

mxmh |>
  group_by(frequency_classical) |>
  select(frequency_classical, anxiety, age) |>
  summarize(across(where(is.numeric),
            list("Mean"   = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "SD"     = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "Min"    = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "Median" = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "Max"    = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .names = "{.fn}_{.col}")
  )

#WIP!! psych option may be better for stacking
#fyi, describe.by creates to a list with 1 df for each x 
mxmh |>
  select(anxiety, age) |>
  psych::describe() |>
  select(vars, n, mean, sd, min, median, max )
```
